_comment: W22-BRIDGE-SIGNPOST-0904, closure plan CL-B3's in-rules half. The South Bridge checkpoint's posted body, placed by `scripts/world/south_bridge.gd::_post_sentry` through `scripts/world/village_npcs.gd` -- the same set-dressing spec shape `data/config/relay_site.json`'s 'Relay Sentry' uses: a Team Tether rank on the installed grunt rig, a world position, a facing, a `place_when` gate, and NO `greeting`, so `village_npcs.gd` draws no prompt for him (INTERACT-SWEEP-0903: a body with nothing to say offers nothing). He is dressing; the fight at this crossing is `south_bridge_grunt` in `data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json`, who stands 8m away at (14, 1314) and is untouched.
_comment_frame: Positions are WORLD metres, as every `village_npcs.gd` config is. The crossing's own frame: centre (8, 1330), the village to the north (smaller z), the locked leaf at z=1321.5, the checkpoint archway at z=1321.0; the crossing's local +z is world -x. `tests/smoke_traversal.gd` walks a body straight down x=8 to the gate, so nobody here stands inside |x - 8| < 1.5.

people.name: Bridge Sentry
people._why_palette:
N09-BRIDGE-CHECKPOINT-0905. The landing judge on W22's own checkpoint frames: 'the guard wears none of the faction's red', and in its ranked list of what is still wrong, 'put the faction's red on the guard'. It was right, and the cause is a stale assumption in `npc_ranks.json`: that file's `_comment_oxblood` still describes the grunt rank's body palette as 'a warm rose-red family multiplied onto the grunt rig's own dark tactical texture', but T1-GROUND (2026-08-30) replaced every rank multiply with a NEUTRAL value ladder -- grunt `#dcdcdc`, officer `#eeeeee`, captain `#ffffff` -- to stop a dark multiply crushing an already-dark texture. The faction colour has been carried by the rig's own paint ever since, and measured off `assets/characters/grunt/grunt_lod0_texture_0.png` that paint is oxblood-family but far too dark to read as colour at all: median HSV hue 340 degrees, saturation 0.35, VALUE 0.173. A neutral 0.86x multiply on top leaves the rendered uniform at value 0.149 and saturation 0.250 -- a near-black smear, which is exactly what the judge saw.

This is a per-INDIVIDUAL override on the one body this lane owns (`village_npcs.gd::model_config` lays `palette` over the rank block, the same five override keys a trainer entry takes), NOT a change to the grunt rank: repainting every Team Tether body in the game is a cast-wide decision two blind rounds have already tuned, and it is not this lane's to make.

The tint SATURATES without darkening. A palette entry is an albedo multiply and can only ever darken, so the red channel is held at full (255) and only green and blue are cut; value stays at the texture's own 0.173 rather than falling to the 0.149 the neutral ladder leaves.

ROUND 1 used `#ffab9c` and landed the rendered uniform at hue 4.9, saturation 0.541, value 0.173 (against hue 0 / 0.250 / 0.149 before). A fresh code-blind judge measured that in the frame and confirmed the direction -- guard torso red-to-blue ratio 1.22 before, 1.72 after -- but still called it 'a warm brown, not oxblood', and gave the target by measuring the banners beside him in the same frame at 3.35. ROUND 2 is set against that number rather than a guess, and it took two passes to land because the arithmetic under-predicts what the tonemap does. First pass `#ff7a5c` (tint red-to-blue 2.77) predicted a 3.71 albedo ratio and RENDERED at 2.40 against the banners' 3.30 in the same frame -- better than round 1's 1.76 and still short. Rendered ratio tracks tint ratio at roughly 0.87x through this lighting, so the second pass scales for it: `#ff6943`, tint red-to-blue 3.81, predicted rendered ~3.3. Predicted albedo hue 8.3, saturation 0.80, value 0.173 -- the same family as the two staked banners (`south_bridge.gd`'s FACTION_CLOTH `#633128`, hue 8 as rendered) and still a DARK uniform rather than a bright red one, because the value never moved: the red channel is pinned at 255 and only green and blue come down, so the multiply can only ever take saturation, never add light.
people._why_here: Crossing-local (-10.8, +1.6): 1.8m in front of the archway on the road's east shoulder, 1.6m off the centreline (clear of the smoke walk and of the road's own 1.5m half-width), under the lantern at local (-10.5, +2.0) and inside the two staked banners at local z=+-2.7 -- so from the approach the body, the light and the cloth read as one post. 8.0m from the `south_bridge_grunt` challenger at (14, 1314) and outside his 4.2m challenge radius, so the two never contest a prompt. `base: grunt_b` so he is not a silhouette twin of the challenger's `grunt_a` in the same frame. `facing_deg` -5: turned back up the road toward the village bend at (11, 1270), at whoever is coming.

place_when._why: A posted sentry belongs to a held crossing. Once the player has genuinely opened the gate the checkpoint is beaten; the barricade, banners and lantern stay as the evidence it was held, but a body still standing guard over an open gate would contradict the leaf that just swung. Same shape as the relay's sentries leaving a dead station.
